title: Hearne and Matonabbee to the Coppermine River, 1770–72
summary: After two failed starts, Hearne left Fort Prince of Wales on 7 December 1770 with Matonabbee and a Chipewyan party. They crossed the Barrenlands and reached the Coppermine River on 14 July 1771, and the Arctic coast at its mouth on 17 July. On the way back Hearne crossed Great Slave Lake in midwinter; he reached the fort in June 1772. He wrote of the killing of Inuit by the Chipewyan at Bloody Falls.

events.label: Bloody Falls and the Arctic coast
events.text: Near the river's mouth the Chipewyan under Matonabbee fell on an Inuit camp and killed some twenty people. Hearne, who could not stop it, wrote it down. Whether his count is exact is not known; the place is now called Bloody Falls.
